name: Catapult Lot
address: 450 E Main St & 203 N Massachusetts Ave, Lakeland, FL 33801
description: Concept rendering only, not a proposed project. A 1.01-acre surface lot facing Lake Mirror beside Catapult, zoned for buildings up to 120 feet (about 10 stories) with roughly 176 apartments plus ground-floor retail, and no on-site parking required. The Amtrak station is a short walk east along Main Street.
zoning: C-6 Downtown Commercial; Urban Center (UCT) context; Future Land Use RAC; Downtown CRA; not in a local historic district
max_height: 120 ft (~10 stories: 16 ft retail + 9 x 10.5 ft residential); min 24 ft street facade; no LDC height bonus
by_right_sqft: ~215,500 GSF (39,511 sf ground floor + 176 units x 1,000 GSF); FAR 5.0 cap = 219,505 sf. With 75% minimum lot coverage, FAR works out to ~6-7 stories average, or a podium plus a slimmer tower to reach 120 ft
parking: None required: inside Downtown Parking Exempt Area. Lot now provides ~100 spaces used by Catapult; replacement parking is a tenant/business issue. Parking garage = conditional use in C-6.
flood_zone: Lot outside mapped SFHA (Zone X), but Lake Mirror's AE zone (BFE 132.4 ft NAVD) lies ~30-60 m from parcel 009021. Get a survey/FIRMette and set finished floor accordingly.
opportunity_zone: Census tract 12105016400 (tract 164): current 2018 Opportunity Zone, in effect through 12/31/2028, but NOT nominated for OZ 2.0 (new zones start 1/1/2027). Treat OZ as a closing window, not a selling point.
cra: Downtown CRA. Precedents: Peachtree Flats TIF rebate = 75% of City+County increment for 5 yrs after CO, plus up to $775k site/infrastructure reimbursement; Onicx (Oak St, 2022) = 80% yrs 1-5 / 60% yrs 6-10 plus fee help. LDDA Curb Appeal grant (50% match) for storefront items.
impact_fees: City water $2,705.02 + wastewater $3,446.03 = $6,151.05 per multifamily unit inside city (FY26-27, Res. 24-064/24-065) -> ~$1,082,585 for 176 units; commercial space billed per gpd ($11.09 water / $14.12 wastewater) set by the Capacity Review Committee. Polk County fees collected in Lakeland add roughly $11,016/MF unit incl. $8,055 school fee (third-party compilation, Aug 2026; verify with Polk County). City offers impact-fee financing (4 yrs) for commercial projects with $400k+ water/wastewater fees.
water_sewer: City Water Utilities; no recorded City easements cross either parcel per City easement layer. Main sizes/capacity need availability request + capacity application.
electric: Lakeland Electric (municipal) service territory. New service starts with LE Energy Delivery Engineering's Commercial Project Application (site + electrical CAD, load data); CIAC may apply; downtown service is typically underground. Economic Development Riders (EDIR-1: 350 kW+ and 25+ new FTEs, 25%->5% discount over 5 yrs; EDIR-2 smaller loads) fit office/commercial users, not apartments. System context: record 792 MW peak (Feb 2026); OUC power-purchase deal extended through 12/31/2027. No public feeder/substation capacity data; ask LE.
fiber: City-owned fiber network (~330-350 mi) commercialized by Summit Broadband; downtown in service area. Building-level availability not published; ask Summit/City.
stormwater: Lot is already almost entirely paved, so a building generally does not add impervious area, but redevelopment still needs City Public Works stormwater review and likely a SWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit (new statewide stormwater rule in effect since 2024). Downtown projects usually use underground vaults; CRA reimbursed underground stormwater for Peachtree Flats. City stormwater utility fee applies to impervious area. Near Lake Mirror, so discharge/treatment standards for the lake may matter.
approvals_needed: LDDA Board design review (C-6); site plan; unity of title/replat to combine 2 parcels (a newly created lot over the 30,000 sf maximum lot area needs staff interpretation or waiver); CSX rail line along the north edge (noise/vibration, railroad coordination for construction). Live Local Act path (F.S. 166.04151(7)): with 40% of units affordable (<=120% AMI) for 30 yrs, City must allow height up to the tallest allowed within 1 mile (C-6 = 120 ft nearby), FAR up to 7.5 (150% of 5.0), administrative approval; density stays capped at 175 du/ac, so it adds height/flexibility, not units.
open_questions: Board/owner appetite (LEDC-affiliated owner). FDEP ACTIVE petroleum cleanup at Firestone #1946, 202 N Massachusetts Ave (remedial action underway, status updated Oct 2025) on or right next to the lot, so get a Phase I/II and ask FDEP about plume extent. Flood elevation. Utility capacity calls.
